title: Four units per lot and inclusionary zoning exemption
subtitle: Also: a nomination of the CAO to the AMO board and a recess between in-camera and public sessions.
overview: Council allowed up to four homes on lots that already permit a single detached, semi-detached or street-townhouse dwelling. The change amends the Official Plan and both zoning by-laws. It goes to the Region of Waterloo for approval {{vote:m4}}. Staff must report back by fall 2025 on how many four-unit homes, including additional dwelling units, have been built.

Council also exempted 97-101 Park Street and 186-194 Victoria Street South from the inclusionary zoning rules approved the week before {{vote:m2}}. Staff had recommended applying the citywide approach. Council instead kept the affordable housing arrangement it approved for the site in June 2023. Two councillors declared conflicts because they own property nearby and took no part in the discussion or votes.

Council nominated its Chief Administrative Officer for Secretary-Treasurer of the AMO Board of Directors for 2024-2026 {{vote:m3}}. The meeting recessed after the in-camera authorization and reconvened that evening. The mayor said an item left over from the closed session will be the first item at the next caucus meeting.

decisions.detail: Council adopted an Official Plan amendment and amended zoning by-laws 85-1 and 2019-051 to permit up to four dwelling units on lots allowing single, semi-detached or street-townhouse homes, with a staff report back by fall 2025.

decisions.item: Inclusionary zoning exemption for Park and Victoria
decisions.detail: Council approved site-specific Official Plan and zoning amendments exempting 97-101 Park Street and 186-194 Victoria Street South from inclusionary zoning, as amended, and waived further notice.
Council nominated the Chief Administrative Officer for Secretary-Treasurer of the AMO Board of Directors for 2024-2026, including reasonable expenses.
Council gave third reading to the by-laws putting the four-unit and Park and Victoria inclusionary zoning amendments into effect, with the two conflicted councillors not taking part in the latter.

debate: A delegate for the property owner opposed the staff recommendation and supported the site-specific alternative. The delegate said council had agreed to an affordable housing arrangement for the site and endorsed it again in June 2023. The alternative includes a sunset of up to five years.
The delegate said the owner would still honour the earlier commitments if a project moves forward in the next couple of years.
Staff recommended a consistent citywide and regionwide approach to inclusionary zoning, as council had approved the week before for all properties in the protected major transit station areas.

One councillor asked how many other approved but unbuilt developments could be pulled into the new framework. Staff said sites with complete site plan, condominium or building permit applications are exempt under transition rules. This site has an approval but is awaiting final regional approval and cannot yet apply for site plan.
One councillor said they disliked the existing affordability terms but felt council should honour the earlier agreement.
